newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China strongman era over, Singapore paper says.
newsitem.headline: China strongman era over, Singapore paper says.

text.p: Singapore's elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew called Deng Xiaoping the man who saved China and the island's leading newspaper said on Friday Deng's death may mark the last time China is ruled by a strongman.
"In his time, a strong grip on power stood as the difference between anarchy and a fighting chance for social progress," The Straits Times newspaper said in an editorial.
"His death on Wednesday, at age 92, also brings down the curtain on possibly the last episode of strongman rule in China," it said.
"Rule by fiat had been a mixed blessing, and conditions in a modernising China almost certainly will make a replication impossible," it added.
Lee said Deng saved China from the kind of disintegration that finished off the Soviet Union.
"He saved China. Without him, China could have been like the Soviet Union. Instead China will become a huge heavyweight nation in 30 years," Lee said in a statement.

The Straits Times said Deng was "one of the great men of the 20th century" and could one day be judged "China's most inspired leader" despite his 1989 crackdown on pro-democracy activists in Tiananmen Square.

"The results of his economic reforms will be beneficial, not just for China, but the entire global community too and will be felt well into the 21st century in every country where goods will be made and sold," the editorial said.
It said the Tiananmen Square crackdown could be justified by reasons of national security, but was a "blot on his record" and added that Deng's failure to relax controls was a mistake.

"The one regret about Deng is that his judgment, perhaps coloured by an atavistic fear of chaos, did not allow him to relax political and social control even as the southern regions became capitalistic in all but name," the newspaper said.

"That had allowed corruption and crime to thrive and local satraps to ride roughshod over small-town folk. People's basic rights, especially in the farming interior, are being short-changed," it added.
"Deng's successors should be alive to the danger."
Earlier, Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said the legacy of the paramount leader would be a "strong and prosperous China".
Goh, who met Deng several times, described him as one of the world's great leaders who "saw events in historical sweep, and thought in terms of generations".
